sites.ownership: The Source Control controller owns the sidebar state behind one Rc<RefCell>.
sites.justification: Refresh, commit, stage, unstage, and diff callbacks all complete asynchronously on the main loop and need one cancellable, generation-aware UI state owner.

sites.ownership: The Source Control tree owns a replaceable weak handle to the sidebar state.
sites.justification: The virtual ListView factory is created before the controller Rc exists; row action buttons need a weak state handle once construction finishes without keeping the window alive.

sites.ownership: The Source Control tree activation hook borrows the controller weak state handle.
sites.justification: ListView activation resolves the current raw Git path and dispatches to the live sidebar state only if the controller still exists.

sites.ownership: The Source Control tree tracks a per-widget activation re-entrancy guard.
sites.justification: Stage/unstage click handlers and list activation share one guard so row buttons do not trigger a duplicate file-open action.

sites.ownership: The Source Control tree factory shares the replaceable weak state handle with row setup and bind callbacks.
sites.justification: Recycled virtual rows need current sidebar state access for button sensitivity and tooltips without rebuilding the factory on every refresh.

sites.ownership: Row factory setup passes the activation guard to action buttons.
sites.justification: Row button callbacks and list activation share the same guard to prevent duplicated activations.

sites.ownership: Source Control row setup borrows the shared weak state slot for per-row action buttons.
sites.justification: Buttons are connected once per recycled row and look up the current TreeListRow path at click time, avoiding stale entry captures.

sites.ownership: Row setup carries the activation guard into each action row.
sites.justification: Row setup wires button callbacks to the shared guard state so list activations can be suppressed while row actions run.

sites.ownership: Source Control action buttons borrow the shared weak state slot.
sites.justification: Stage and unstage clicks must dispatch to the live sidebar state without owning it or using row indexes.

sites.ownership: Row action buttons toggle a guard before running sidebar actions.
sites.justification: The shared guard is shared across all action buttons so list row activation and button activation cannot double-trigger.

sites.ownership: Source Control activation dispatch borrows the controller weak state handle.
sites.justification: File and folder activation must avoid keeping the sidebar alive after teardown while still resolving actions against the current snapshot.

sites.ownership: The typed Git process boundary owns the Gio subprocess pipe flags.
sites.justification: V9 allows subprocess use only here to run bundled /app/bin/git with typed operations, no shell, bounded output, fixed env, and reviewable argv construction.

sites.ownership: The typed Git process boundary owns stdout capture for sandbox Git.
sites.justification: Git status, attributes, blob reads, and commit responses are bounded and parsed only through this reviewed runner.

sites.ownership: The typed Git process boundary owns stderr capture for sandbox Git.
sites.justification: Captured stderr is size-capped and mapped to user-facing errors without exposing a generic command runner.

sites.ownership: The typed Git process boundary owns subprocess creation.
sites.justification: All Git subprocess invocations go through the allowlisted operation methods in this file and use bundled /app/bin/git, no host PATH lookup, no shell, and deterministic environment overrides.

sites.ownership: The Git process tests own a one-shot callback result slot.
sites.justification: Typed Git operations report through Rc callbacks; the test slot captures immediate callback results without sharing state outside the test.

sites.ownership: The Git process async tests own a one-shot callback result slot.
sites.justification: The helper pumps the GLib main context until the typed Git callback completes and removes pending timeout sources before leaving the test.
